movement_source: row 'Net interest margin (%)', column 31 Dec 24 column -> column 31 Dec 25 column
headline: CBA's Group net interest margin fell 4 basis points in 1H26 (Dec 25) to 2.04% from 2.08% in 1H25 (Dec 24), per the results book KPI table (continuing operations basis). Excluding growth in liquid assets, which the bank says have broadly neutral impacts on net interest income, NIM decreased by 1 basis point. The results book's walk (Dec 24 Half to Dec 25 Half) attributes the -4 bps to: Liquids -3, Asset pricing -2, Funding costs -3, Portfolio mix +1, Basis risk 0, Capital/Replicating & Other +6, Treasury & Markets -3. The presentation's 12-month Group margin walk corroborates the same -4 bps (208 to 204) with a slightly different framing: Liquids & repos -4, Asset pricing -2, Funding costs -3, Portfolio mix +1, Interest rate risk hedging +6, Treasury & Markets -2.

drivers.narrative: Liquids reduced margin by 3 bps. The bank notes growth in liquid assets has broadly neutral impacts on net interest income, and the presentation attributes the drag to a +$20bn increase in average liquid assets in 1H26 vs 1H25.

Asset pricing reduced margin by 2 bps: home lending pricing down 2 bps and business lending pricing down 1 bp reflecting elevated competition, partly offset by higher consumer finance margins up 1 bp.
Funding costs reduced margin by 3 bps, driven by declining interest rates, unfavourable deposit mix and increased deposit price competition.
Portfolio mix increased margin by 1 bp, driven by favourable funding mix from strong growth in at-call deposits.
Basis risk was flat, contributing 0 bps to the movement.
Capital, Replicating and Other increased margin by 6 bps: replicating portfolio up 5 bps due to changes in portfolio rate and volume, and higher earnings on capital hedges up 1 bp.

Treasury and Markets reduced margin by 3 bps due to higher funding costs in Carbon and Commodities and Global Markets (offset in other operating income) and an increase in reverse sale and repurchase agreement balances.

disagreements.topic: NIM walk framing between results book and presentation
disagreements.explanation: Both documents show the same -4 bps total (208 to 204) and the same Asset pricing -2, Funding costs -3, Portfolio mix +1, and +6 for capital/replicating. The presentation groups institutional repos into 'Liquids & repos' (-4) and reports Treasury & Markets at -2, whereas the book reports Liquids at -3 and Treasury & Markets at -3 (repos included there). Net effect identical.

limitations: The results book's walk (page 28) is adopted as the primary framing per the walk-preference rule; the presentation's walk (page 59) corroborates the same -4 bps total but groups repos differently (Liquids & repos -4 vs book's Liquids -3 and Treasury & Markets -3).
The Group NIM row carries no cash or statutory label; it is reported on the bank's primary (cash) basis and on a continuing operations basis per the table header.
The bank's stated reason for each driver is taken verbatim from the results book narrative; no additional reason is supplied.
